title: Creative Project Manager (YouTube+ Short-Form Distribution) - Remote
description:
At Novakid, we are on a mission to build the world’s best online education platform for children. With over 100,000 students and 4,000 teachers, Novakid is already one of the most popular language learning platforms for children aged 4-12 across Europe and Asia.
About the role
We are building a new interactive entertainment project for families (parents + children) - with YouTube as the main platform and content home.
Short-form content (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) will serve as the acquisition engine: hooks, teasers, cliffhangers, and emotional moments designed to drive viewers to the main YouTube episodes.
You will own the creative direction for both long-form and short-form - ensuring every piece of content works together as a system, not separately.
Before we invest in full production, we will first test concepts using short-form content to measure audience demand, engagement, and intent to watch longer episodes.
Cultural & Audience Insight

• Ensure concepts resonate with parents culturally and emotionally, with a focus on the TR market

• Anticipate cross-cultural interpretation, humor, and sensitivity

• Keep Novakid relevant to real parent conversations, not marketing narratives

What you have done before (real experience we need)

• You have concepted and led production of long-form YouTube content (8-20+ min) - episodic, story-driven, with clear hooks and payoff.

• You have successfully repurposed long-form content into short-form trailers/teasers that drove measurable traffic back to YouTube.

• You have tested content concepts using only short-form (TikTok, Reels, Shorts) before investing in full episodes - and can show examples of how you made that decision.

• You understand YouTube organic metrics (CTR, retention, AVD) and short-form metrics (completion rate, shares, comments) - and how they relate.

• You have worked on projects with participatory or community elements (even simple ones like comments shaping next steps).

Key responsibilities

• YouTube first: Everything starts with the long-form episode. Short-form serves it, not the other way around.

• Test fast: Use short-form to validate concepts before building full episodes.

• Own the creative vision from title/thumbnail to final frame of each episode.

• Collaborate with production teams but stay responsible for viral instincts and audience psychology.

• Analyze performance across both formats and iterate quickly.

Requirements
Must-have qualifications

• Portfolio with long-form YouTube content you concepted (show retention, CTR, or growth if possible).

• Proven ability to drive traffic from short-form to long-form (examples required).

• Deep understanding of TikTok, Reels, and YouTube Shorts as acquisition tools, not standalone entertainment.

• Obsessed with hooks, pacing, cliffhangers, and payoff.

• Strong interest in parenting, family dynamics, or human stories involving children

Requirements:

• Experience leading video projects from concept to final delivery.

• Experience with family, parenting, or kids content.

• Basic editing or thumbnail design sense.

• Experience building a YouTube channel (other Social Media channels) from zero.

• C1 level English

We offer:

• Opportunity to work in an innovative, fast-growing edtech company.

• A creative and collaborative work environment.

• Comprehensive professional development and leadership growth opportunities.

• The chance to have a meaningful impact on the lives of young learners around the world.

• 100% Remote work

• Unlimited holidays

• Bonuses and stock options

title: Chief Sales Officer
description:
A high-ticket B2C business is hiring a Chief Sales Officer to take full ownership of its sales organisation and scale it well beyond where it sits today.
The business turns over the equivalent of around R16 million a month across roughly 160 front-end sales. The sales function works. It is not where it needs to be, and that is the job.
You will report directly to the CEO. The Sales Team Lead, who is also the strongest closer in the business, reports to you and stays in his seat on his existing structure. Closers and setters sit beneath him. The structure is CEO, then you, then the Sales Team Lead, then the closers and setters.
This is not a role for someone stepping up into the biggest job of their career. The business wants someone who has already run a larger and more sophisticated sales organisation than this one, and who can bring that experience, those systems and that thinking in with them.
WHAT YOU WILL OWN
Overall sales strategy and the performance of the whole sales organisation.
Managing, mentoring and developing the Sales Team Lead.
Close rates, sales volume and revenue.
KPI analysis, and finding the constraints holding performance back.
Forecasting and performance reporting to the CEO.
Sales process, scripts, objection handling and methodology.
The call review, coaching and training systems.
Diagnosing individual weakness across closers and setters, and fixing it.
Standards, accountability and energy across the sales floor.
Future recruitment and capacity planning.
The management structure and systems needed to scale significantly.
Working directly with the CEO on sales strategy and growth.
The question you will answer continuously: what is stopping this business performing at the next level, and what has to change to get it there?
Requirements
WHAT YOU MUST HAVE
10 years plus in sales, with significant time at senior leadership level. Ideally you have held the title of Chief Sales Officer, VP of Sales, Sales Director or a very senior Head of Sales.
You have managed Sales Managers or Team Leads, not only individual salespeople. This is the deal breaker. Managing closers directly is not the same job and will not be enough here.
You have run a sales organisation materially larger than this one. Be ready to state the revenue you carried, the headcount and the structure.
Specific, evidenced performance improvements you personally drove. A number, an intervention, a before and an after.
You have built the systems, not just used them. Call review, coaching cadence, scripts, objection handling, forecasting, KPI reporting. Designed by you, not inherited.
Fully remote-ready. Fibre, backup power, a working camera and a quiet space, and you can hold UK working hours permanently.
NICE TO HAVE
High-ticket B2C experience, particularly coaching, education, consulting or something comparable.
Experience taking a team through a step change in volume, not steady-state management.
Previous experience working remotely into a UK business.
THE PACKAGE
R60,000 to R65,000 per month basic, plus a performance commission on every front-end sale above the current baseline of 160 per month. As a guide, at 200 sales a month the commission is around R9,400 a month. At 250 it is around R21,000. At 300 it is around R33,000. On that basis, realistic earnings at 250 sales a month are roughly R83,000 per month. The baseline is reviewed periodically as the business grows.
Full-time and permanent. Fully remote from anywhere in South Africa, on UK working hours.
HOW TO APPLY
In your application, answer these directly: the largest sales organisation you have managed, in revenue and in headcount; how many Sales Managers or Team Leads reported to you and for how long; and one performance improvement you personally drove, with the number before and the number after. Applications that do not answer all three will not get past the first read.

The Performance team is focused on building deep diagnostic tools and performing high-level analysis to reduce latency,  infrastructure costs and increase services efficiency.

You will be responsible for leading complex performance investigations, identifying systemic bottlenecks, and driving efficiency across one of the largest JVM-based microservice architectures in the world.

Our core principles and behaviors include ownership, simplicity, veracity-first, teamwork, and a focus on quality over quantity. During a normal work day, you will interact with critical infrastructure layers, from the Linux Kernel and JVM internals to cloud-wide orchestration.

- Strategic Collaboration: Work closely with the Computing Squad to align orchestration strategies with system performance goals, ensuring a seamless interface between infrastructure and workloads.

title: Southeastern Idaho Environmental Specialist
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo!  We are searching for a Southeastern Idaho Environmental Specialist to join our engineering team.

Position Description

Oklo is seeking an Environmental Specialist to support environmental compliance, field oversight, permitting coordination, procedure development, and environmental stewardship activities associated with nuclear and industrial development projects in southeastern Idaho.

This role will work closely with construction, operations, licensing, engineering, and regulatory teams to ensure environmental compliance across active project sites and related field activities. The position requires field presence and direct interaction with contractors, regulators, and internal stakeholders.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, field-oriented, technically capable, and comfortable operating in dynamic construction and industrial environments with high standards for safety and documentation. Additionally, the candidate must be a strong technical writing capable of producing technical procedures for supporting meeting Oklo’s environmental stewardship and compliance requirements.

Specific responsibilities may include:

• Manage regular meetings with partners such as Batelle Energy Alliance (BEA) and the Department of Energy Idaho (DOE-ID)

• Work with Oklo subject matter experts to track documentation related to environmental authorizations, approvals, and permits for projects in Southeast Idaho

• Conduct environmental field inspections and compliance assessments at active project and construction sites

• Interpret environmental requirements and support implementation of environmental compliance programs, permits, and site environmental procedures

• Monitor internal Oklo teams and contractor compliance with environmental requirements and best management practices (BMPs)

• Assist with stormwater, erosion and sediment control, dust control, spill prevention, and waste management oversight

• Coordinate environmental monitoring activities including water, air, soil, and waste tracking as needed

• Support preparation and maintenance of environmental reports, inspection logs, permit documentation, and corrective actions

• Identify environmental compliance issues and implement corrective actions.

• Assist with spill response activities, investigations, and follow-up actions

• Interface with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies when required

• Coordinate with engineering, construction, procurement, subcontracts, operations, and other teams to ensure environmental requirements are incorporated into project planning and execution

• Track and communicate environmental compliance risks and emerging issues

• Support environmental audits, readiness reviews, and corrective action programs

• Help maintain environmental documentation systems and records

• Participate in field walkdowns, project meetings, and environmental planning discussions

• Travel periodically to project and operational locations within Idaho and surrounding regions as needed

• Familiarity with State of Idaho, Bonneville County, Bingham County and City of Idaho Falls environmental regulations

• Promote environmental awareness and continuous improvement initiatives.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Biology, Ecology, or a related technical discipline

• 3+ years of experience supporting environmental compliance, construction environmental oversight, industrial operations, or related field activities

• Familiarity with environmental regulations and permitting requirements including:

• Clean Water Act

• Stormwater permitting

• Spill prevention and response

• Hazardous waste management

• Air quality and environmental compliance programs

• Experience performing environmental inspections and documenting findings

• Strong technical writing and reporting skills

• Ability to work safely in active industrial and construction environments

We're looking for a Finance Systems Lead to own and evolve the systems that support Baseten's finance operations, including ERP, planning tools, and the broader finance and adjacent systems stack, spanning HRIS/payroll, CPQ, and commissions, as we implement, integrate, and automate across them.

As Baseten scales, so does the number of systems finance depends on and touches, from the ERP to planning to compensation and quote to cash tooling. This role exists to bring a dedicated owner to that stack, someone who can lead implementations (partnering with contractors or vendor CSMs for hands-on technical configuration where needed), keep systems integrated and clean as we grow, and find automation opportunities that save the team time.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You will partner with Accounting, FP&A, People, Sales and Revenue Operations, Legal, and IT to understand how each team uses its systems, and design integrations and workflows that serve the business without creating more manual work.

Core Finance Systems

- Own finance systems strategy, configuration, and roadmap, partnering with contractors or vendor CSMs on hands-on technical configuration as needed

- Lead the implementation and ongoing administration of our finance systems and tools

- Own finance system integrations end to end, ensuring clean data flow between ERP, planning, billing, and other systems, partnering with contractors or vendor CSMs on hands-on technical configuration as needed

Cross-Functional Systems

- Partner with People on HRIS and payroll systems, ensuring accurate data flow between HRIS, payroll, and ERP

- Partner with Sales and Revenue Operations on CPQ and commission systems, ensuring pricing, quoting, and commission calculations tie cleanly back to billing and revenue recognition

- Serve as a systems thought partner across finance-adjacent tools, even in areas where another team owns day to day administration

Automation and Process Improvement

- Identify and build automation across manual finance workflows, from data reconciliation to reporting, partnering with the Data Analytics team where relevant

- Evaluate new tools and system enhancements as the company scales, and build the business case for investment

- Document system architecture and workflows so institutional knowledge does not live in one person's head

Governance and Controls

- Manage system access, permissions, and controls in partnership with Accounting and IT

- Support audit requests related to systems and automated controls

REQUIREMENTS

- 7+ years of experience in finance systems, business systems, or related systems administration role

- Experience implementing or administering a financial planning tool

- Experience integrating systems across finance and adjacent functions, such as HRIS/payroll or CPQ/commissions

- Strong technical aptitude, with the ability to build automation and workflows and to direct contractors or vendor CSMs on hands-on configuration work

- Strong cross-functional partnership skills, able to work with Accounting, FP&A, People, Sales and Revenue Operations, and Legal to design systems and workflows that serve each team's needs

- Comfortable operating as a systems generalist across a broad stack, not a single-tool specialist

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

Axon’s federal market team seeks a customer-obsessed Mission Success Manager who consistently overdelivers. Our federal public safety customers operate in high-stakes environments with challenging missions, and they need a trusted partner who can turn complex problems into meaningful outcomes.

As a Mission Success Manager, you will be that partner. You will own a portfolio of Axon’s most important federal customers, develop a deep understanding of each customer’s mission, and take accountability for their success. You will bring together the best of Axon to solve hard problems, ensure our technology delivers real operational value, and build partnerships that make Axon indispensable to the missions you support.

 

What You’ll Do

Location: Boston, NYC or Washington DC Area preferred
Reports to: Director, Customer Solutions
Direct Reports: 0
Travel expectation is 50%

•
You own mission success. You are accountable for your customers’ success with Axon-from delivering their programs effectively to driving adoption, value realization, and continuous improvement. You connect what Axon delivers to the outcomes your customers need to achieve.

•
You are the customer’s trusted partner. Build strong relationships with stakeholders from day-to-day operators to senior executives. Earn their trust by being responsive, candid, and reliable, and become the person they turn to when they have a challenge, an idea, or need help navigating Axon.

•
You make complex programs run effectively. Manage scope, schedule, cost, dependencies, and risk across your portfolio. Bring clarity to ambiguity, proactively remove obstacles, and ensure commitments turn into outcomes.

•
You orchestrate Axon around the customer. Work across Sales, Deployment, Technical Support, Product, Engineering, and other teams to deliver what the customer needs. You know who to engage, when to engage them, and how to drive alignment across organizational boundaries.

•
The misses keep you up at night. Anticipate problems before they become escalations and take ownership when things go wrong. Identify recurring pain points and emerging customer needs, drive them toward resolution, and ensure lessons learned turn into action.

•
You know how your decisions impact the business. Understand how decisions around product scope, services, costing, scheduling, and contract structure affect both customer outcomes and company performance. Identify opportunities where Axon can solve additional customer needs and partner with Sales to grow and scale the relationship.

•
You have a low ego, high impact attitude. You set a high bar for yourself, bring recommendations instead of just problems, and do whatever is needed to drive the right outcome. You are excited by being an individual contributor because it gives you the opportunity to solve hard problems and make a measurable impact.

•
5+ years supporting complex federal customers or programs - Experience in federal program management, customer success, professional services, consulting, or a similar customer-facing role is strongly preferred.

•
Deep customer and mission orientation - You seek to understand what the customer is trying to accomplish, why it matters, and what success looks like.

Strong program management skills - You can manage complex scope, schedules, dependencies, risks, stakeholders, and commitments across multiple workstreams.

title: Practice Manager – Paediatric Hearing & Allied Health
description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Our client is an Australian paediatric hearing services business that assesses children's hearing across clinic, school and home-visit settings, and delivers a growing program of hearing screenings in schools across NSW (expanding to 30-40 schools next year). Billing is mostly through Medicare and private patients, with a small but growing number of NDIS-funded families. The business is led by its Practice Owner, who this role reports to directly, supported by a small team of audiologists and casual screeners.

ABOUT THE ROLE

• A full-time Practice Manager role - in Australian healthcare, this sits above a medical receptionist, owning the administrative and operational back end of the clinic (patient and referral administration, reporting, scheduling and compliance) rather than front-desk reception duties.

• The role is split across two core areas: day-to-day patient and referral administration in the practice's patient management system, and end-to-end coordination of the school hearing screening program - from first enquiry through to the results summary sent back to each school.

• This role is trusted with genuinely confidential information - referrals, clinical reports, Medicare and patient details, and student data - so accuracy and discretion matter on every task, not just the obvious ones.

• This role is not asked to just follow instructions - it's expected to review its own work, ask questions, and genuinely learn a process once rather than needing it re-taught.

• Day to day, this role works independently across several systems (a patient/practice management system, Excel, Outlook, Canva, SharePoint) and will regularly hit things that don't quite fit the standard process - a missing referral, a doctor not yet in the system, a parent's booking details not matching their child's. The right person investigates and resolves what they can before escalating, rather than deferring every question upward.

• There's a lighter, ongoing layer of practice support on top of this - scheduling and rostering audiologists and casual screeners, social media content, SOP updates and compliance record-keeping - that adds variety without taking priority over the patient and school-screening workload.

PRIMARY PURPOSE

To independently and accurately manage patient and referral administration, and to coordinate the school hearing screening program end to end - on schedule, with genuine attention to detail and confidentiality - while escalating only genuine exceptions rather than routine questions.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

title: AI Resilience Partner
description:
EQL Tech is partnered with Convergent Research in the search for an outstanding AI Resilience Partner. Convergent Research is a nonprofit science studio best known for pioneering the Focused Research Organization (FRO): purpose-built, mission-driven orgs designed to solve technological bottlenecks, unlock whole new fields, and lead to scaled revolutions. We’ve proven our model works by building over 14 high-impact scientific organizations spanning AI (here), biotech, mathematics, climate science, and more.
AI capability is compounding faster than the world's ability to absorb it. Other technologies got decades to sort out their safety codes, their testing regimes, and the institutions that enforce them. We don't have decades. The defenses have to be built while the technology is still moving, and there's no budget line anywhere that says build the defenses now.
That's the gap this role exists to close. Not "how do we build another AI company" - plenty of people are doing that. This role is about building the missing institutions and technical infrastructure that make the world resilient to advanced AI: the defensive capabilities that won't be built by a startup, won't fit inside an academic lab, and are too important to leave to chance.
What you’ll do
Partners at Convergent are like senior partners at a venture incubator. You'll create and fully own a growing portfolio of FROs and other scientific projects that advance AI resilience - society's capacity to capture AI's benefits while withstanding its risks.
The portfolio is yours to define, but the surface area is much bigger than model safety alone. It spans defensive biosecurity (pathogen-agnostic detection, next-generation PPE, rapid countermeasures), provably secure cyber-physical systems and formal verification, epistemic infrastructure for a world flooded with AI-generated content, independent evaluation and monitoring capacity, compute governance, economic modeling of the transition - and areas nobody has named yet. The unifying question: what keystone defensive capability, if it existed, would make the world meaningfully harder to break?
You will have extreme latitude to decide what your portfolio should include, and the resources to go build it.
You’ll form strong theses, find extraordinary founders, pressure-test ideas, raise money, build boards, launch organizations, and help them move with the speed and focus of the best deep-tech startups.
Specifically, you will:

• Roadmap the AI resilience landscape to identify the bottlenecks and keystone capabilities worth building organizations around

• Source and diligence ideas for new projects and organizations and design funding calls in partnership with funders

• Build founding teams and help recruit the early hires who will make or break them

• Directly contribute to and coach founders on technical and organizational roadmaps, fundraising, and standing up startup ops from zero

• Serve as a Director on multiple FRO boards, keeping teams on track against milestones and helping founders make the genuinely hard calls on funding, strategic direction, hiring, firing, and operations

• Represent Convergent externally, building high-trust relationships with the philanthropic and public funders now committing serious capital to AI resilience

• Contribute to Convergent-wide initiatives like our Founder Retreats and Residencies

• You have ideas, or a credible plan to find ideas, for large-scale efforts that would measurably improve how the world weathers this transition

title: Principal Product Manager, Payments
description:
Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.

Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.

Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.

As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.

We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.

Role Overview
We're looking for an experienced Principal Product Manager to lead the strategy and execution of the payments platform and experiences that help drive the accelerated growth we’ve experienced across our Grading and Marketplace business lines, including our Liquidity offerings and Digital Repacking product ( Power Packs ).
Money movement sits underneath nearly everything Collectors does. Every grading submission, vault transaction, marketplace sale, consignment payout, among other transactional experiences relies on a payment stack that has to be fast, resilient, cost-effective and compliant across a growing number of business models and expanding globally. This role will own that stack outright: how funds come in, how funds go out, how they are routed and how customers see and control their money in our products.
You will work with stakeholders across our Marketplace and Grading business lines, Finance and Treasury, Legal, Compliance, Risk, as well as other Product and Tech partner teams, with regular exposure to the executive team.
What You'll Do

• Own the payments strategy and roadmap. Set a multi-year direction for the payment platform that serves today's revenue lines and anticipates the ones we haven't launched yet. Sequence platform investment against near-term business commitments and defend those tradeoffs with executives.

• Build a wallet that customers can use across our products and platforms. Own balance and activity views, top-up, withdrawal, and split-pay, turning stored value from a settlement mechanism into a reason customers choose us.

• Take payments international. Deliver the payment, currency, and local method capabilities, partnering with Tax and Legal on registration, reporting obligations including DAC7, and market-by-market compliance.

• Run money-in and money-out end to end. Acquiring, alternative payment methods, payouts, settlement, funding patterns, and reconciliation, including the ledger and reporting foundation Finance depends on for accurate, timely close.

• Drive orchestration and cost optimization. Own multi-PSP routing, least-cost routing, failover and redundancy, retry and decline strategy, and network-level economics. Treat authorization rate and cost per transaction as products you are accountable for, not metrics you report on.

• Partner internally with Risk and Fraud teams to reduce payment fraud and dispute loss, transaction screening, chargeback and dispute workflows, and the approval

You should genuinely be part of this world. You know what is trending, who people pay attention to, what feels authentic, and how to identify creators that can make technical products feel exciting and accessible.
At the same time, you know how to build structure around it, creating a program that scales, learning fast from what works, and building something much bigger than one-off campaigns.

• Identify and build relationships with creators who genuinely align with Base44’s product, audience, and brand, including creators that may not be obvious fits at first glance.

• Leverage your deep understanding of the creator landscape to spot emerging voices, cultural trends, and communities that can help shape how Base44 shows up online.

• Build authentic partnerships with creators across YouTube, LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram, and other relevant platforms, creating a strong network around the product.

• Work closely with creators to help shape content that feels authentic to their audience while maximizing reach, engagement, and overall performance.

• Bring a strong understanding of internet culture and creator dynamics to identify the creators, content formats, and narratives that can make a technical product resonate with the right audience.

• Collaborate closely with product, growth, and marketing teams to connect creator activity with product launches, new features, and strategic company moments.

• Build and continuously refine a scalable creator program that allows Base44 to grow creator partnerships in a repeatable and sustainable way.

• Measure what works, learn quickly, and continuously improve how creator partnerships translate into awareness, engagement, and product adoption.

• Hands on experience working in influencer marketing, creator partnerships, or UGC program management at a tech company or startup

• Deep familiarity with the creator ecosystem: platforms, deal structures, creator vetting, content performance metrics, and what "scale" actually looks like

• Experience managing a high volume of creator relationships simultaneously - not just a handful of big names

• Strong operator instincts: fast, organized, and able to close partnerships without a lot of hand-holding

title: GenAI CBRNE Cyber Security Expert

As a GenAI CBRNE & Cyber Red Team Expert, you'll adversarially test and strengthen the safety guardrails of GenAI systems against high-risk cyber threats - with a particular focus on industrial hacking, SCADA systems, ICS/OT environments, and CBRNE domains.
Drawing on deep industrial cybersecurity expertise (hands-on familiarity with SCADA, Modbus, DNP3, and PLC exploits) alongside CBRNE domain knowledge and advanced AI red-teaming skills, you'll design sophisticated adversarial prompts, multi-turn attack scenarios, jailbreaks, and model evaluations to determine when GenAI systems could materially enable physical-world industrial attacks or cyber-enabled CBRNE threats.
The role calls for an adversarial mindset: thinking like a malicious actor to find ways AI systems could be manipulated, combining seemingly benign information across interactions, circumventing safeguards, or exploiting model behavior to extract sensitive cyber-CBRNE information.
Key Responsibilities

• Run rigorous red-teaming of GenAI models across SCADA, ICS, and CBRNE scenarios. You will be probing for safeguard bypasses, dangerous capability escalation, and unintended disclosure of sensitive OT information.

• Design adversarial prompts, jailbreaks, and multi-turn evaluations against industrial hacking scenarios (SCADA, PLCs, DCS, Modbus/DNP3/IEC 60870-5-104/Ethernet-IP, critical infrastructure, hazardous-material facilities).

• Evaluate whether models can be manipulated into assisting attacks via payload generation, ladder logic exploitation, reconnaissance, or aggregating benign inputs into high-risk workflows.

• Document failure modes (obfuscation, role-play, decomposition, escalation), classify severity, and report findings to safety/alignment teams.

• Build repeatable test suites, adversarial datasets, and risk taxonomies; stay current on GenAI attack techniques and CBRNE/critical-infrastructure threats.

Requirements
Requirements

Preferred Qualifications

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack - from the lab to the field - we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

WHO YOU ARE

• Partners with PSO delivery leadership, Sales, and the Mission Engineering/Operator team to align migration/integration capacity and pricing with customer commitments.

A new wave of AI SaaS builders - Lovable, Vercel, Cursor, Bolt, and others - is becoming the default starting point for how software gets built, and each one is standing up its own marketplace or integration directory to connect what people build inside them to real backend services.
I'm hiring a Partner Manager, AI Native Ecosystems to make Customer.io the obvious, pre-integrated messaging and engagement layer for everything built on these platforms. This role sits at the intersection of business development and technical integration work: part of the job is identifying and recruiting the right platforms and negotiating partnership terms; the other part is working hands-on with our Product team to scope and ship the actual integration required to get listed and featured.
AI builder platforms are becoming a new front door for software creation - and a new distribution channel for infrastructure providers. Getting Customer.io natively integrated and well-positioned across this ecosystem now, while the partner programs and technical standards are still forming, is a land-grab opportunity. This role owns that land-grab end to end.
What we value

•
Bias to Action: comfortable building the process, not just executing an existing one - these marketplaces and their rules are new and changing monthly.

•
Cross-Functional Fluency: equally credible in a deal negotiation and a technical scoping conversation with engineers.

•
Ownership: drives a relationship from first contact through signed agreement through shipped integration, without waiting to be handed the next step.

•
Resourcefulness: comfortable operating without a dominant brand - you're earning the meeting, not getting it by default.

What you’ll do

•
Immediate priority: optimize our existing Claude and ChatGPT integrations, including MCP discoverability and GEO (making sure Customer.io shows up when AI tools recommend a messaging/engagement platform).

• Identify and prioritize which AI builder platforms (Vercel, Cursor, Lovable, Bolt, Google, AWS, and others) are worth partnering with, working with Engineering, Design, and Product to assess technical feasibility and distribution potential, including CLI and MCP connector priorities.

• Own the full partner relationship lifecycle - outbound, negotiation, and ongoing management - from first contact through signed agreement through shipped integration.

• Negotiate commercial terms (revenue share, co-marketing, marketplace listing requirements) directly with partner and BD counterparts.

• Translate each marketplace's technical requirements into a spec and work hands-on with our engineering team to scope and ship the integration - you don't need to write the integration yourself, but you need to be fluent enough to unblock it.

• Get Customer.io listed, verified, and ideally featured in each platform's marketplace or directory, and manage the relationship as review guidelines and requirements evolve.

• Track installs, activations, and pipeline sourced from each marketplace; report on which partnerships are driving real usage versus which need renegotiation or deprioritization.

• Build the playbook as you go - there's no existing process for this at Customer.io yet, and part of the job is creating repeatable criteria (target criteria, technical requirements checklist, deal template) so new platforms can be evaluated and onboarded quickly.

What we're looking for

• 5-7 years in business development, partnerships, or platform/ecosystem roles, ideally with a developer tools, API-first, or marketplace-driven

title: Electrical Technician (Power Generation) - Memphis
description:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge.  Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Power Generation team is seeking an Electrical Technician to operate and maintain plant electrical systems at SpaceX’s power generation facility. You will work hands-on across medium-voltage generation, distribution, and balance-of-plant electrical equipment up to 13.5 kV and 34.8 kV. This is an operations and maintenance role - you will switch, troubleshoot, repair, and keep electrical systems online in a high-reliability, fast-paced plant environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Perform operations and maintenance on plant electrical systems, including generators, transformers, switchgear, motor control centers, motors, VFDs, UPS units, automatic transfer switches, and emergency/black-start equipment, at voltages up to 13.5 kV and 34.8 kV.

• Execute switching, isolation, LOTO, racking of breakers, and restoration of medium-voltage equipment in accordance with plant procedures and NFPA 70E.

• Troubleshoot electrical faults on power distribution, protection, grounding, lighting, and auxiliary systems using one-line diagrams, schematics, and electrical test equipment.

• Perform preventive and predictive maintenance, inspections, and repairs to improve reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.

• Support plant startups, shutdowns, outages, and commissioning activities alongside operators, controls technicians, and engineers.

• Install, terminate, and maintain plant electrical equipment, cable, and control wiring as required for operations and maintenance work.

• Respond to electrical alarms, trips, and equipment failures; support root-cause investigations and implement corrective actions.

• Coordinate with operations, engineering, and utility personnel on switching, clearances, and electrical work that affects plant generation.

• Maintain accurate work orders, switching records, and as-found/as-left documentation.

• Follow all safety, LOTO, arc-flash, and PPE requirements while working in energized and hazardous plant environments.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

• 3+ years of experience as an electrical technician, industrial electrician, or similar role maintaining industrial or power generation electrical systems.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience operating and maintaining medium-voltage electrical systems (4.16 kV to 34.8 kV), including switchgear, transformers, and breakers.

• Experience in a power plant, generating station, or other high-reliability industrial facility.

• Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, electrical schematics, and equipment O&M manuals.

• Experience with LOTO, switching procedures, and NFPA 70E / arc-flash safety practices.

• Experience troubleshooting motors, VFDs, MCCs, UPS systems, and plant auxiliary electrical equipment.

• Familiarity with electrical test equipment (multimeters, insulation testers, infrared, and similar).

• Journeyman electrician license or equivalent formal electrical training.

• Experience using a CMMS or work-order system to plan and close maintenance work.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-discipline operations and maintenance team.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

A customer’s fallen behind on a credit card payment. They already know what they owe. What they don't know is whether taking our call means getting further behind, or getting somewhere. title: UK Sales Manager for Children's Online Courses Self-study
description:
What you'll do: Deliver 1:1 online trial lessons, understand each child's needs, recommend the right Kodland program, and help families make a confident enrollment decision.
Schedule: 20-25 hrs/week on average, mostly weekday afternoons/evenings + daytime weekends (UK hours)
Pay: Fixed rate per completed trial + performance bonuses - clear, transparent structure
Support: Live onboarding, guided practice, and a short assessment before you start with real families
If this sounds like your kind of role, here's the full picture 👇
1. About Kodland 👨‍💻👩‍💻
Kodland is an international online school helping kids aged 8-17 build real digital skills - Python, Roblox, Minecraft, Digital Creativity, and more. We work with students and families across the US, Europe, the UK, CIS, Latin America, MENA, and beyond, all through live 1:1 or small-group Zoom classes with a project-based approach.
Our mission: help kids become confident, curious thinkers who are comfortable with technology and problem-solving.
🔗 Learn more about Kodland
2. A Day in the Life of a TCM 🎬
Curious what this actually looks like day to day? This short video shows a typical TCM schedule, how a real trial lesson unfolds, and what the conversation with parents feels like.
👉 Watch it before applying - it's the fastest way to know if this role fits your lifestyle.
3. What You'll Actually Be Doing 🎧
Each trial lesson, you'll:

• Meet the child and at least one parent on Zoom

• Build rapport and ask the right questions to understand the child's background, interests, and goals

• Lead a short hands-on activity (simple coding, game logic, or digital task) using ready-made materials

• Recommend the best-fit program based on what you observe

• Answer questions, address concerns, and guide the family to a clear decision

This role blends three skill sets:
🎓 Teaching - explaining clearly and keeping kids engaged
🗣 Communication - listening well and adapting to each family
💼 Sales - showing value and confidently closing when it's a good fit
This isn't a scripted call-center job. You'll get structure and materials, but you're expected to think on your feet and lead the conversation.
4. Schedule & Availability 🕒

• Weekdays: mainly 14:00-21:00 UK time

• Weekends: mainly 11:00-18:00 UK time

• 5 days/week , with 1 weekday off + 1 weekend day off

Exact hours are negotiable, but we need consistent weekly availability so we can plan ahead and keep families from waiting.
5. Pay & Earning Potential 💶
Independent contractor role, paid twice a month , built on two parts:

• Base pay: €6 per completed trial (up to €7.50 based on your grade)

•
Bonus: 5-10% of your monthly sales - the better your conversion rate, the higher your %

📌 Admin hours are paid at the same rate as trial classes.

What that looks like in real numbers (based on internal averages, part-time):

• 🌱 New to the role: ~€700/month

• 📈 Steady performers: €1,100+/month

• 🏆 Top performers: up to €1,900/month

You'll get regular feedback, coaching, and webinars to help you grow - income increases with skill, consistency, and effort, but it's a real, achievable path even part-time.
Requirements
Must-Haves

• Clear, confident spoken English that US parents can easily follow

• A laptop/PC with working webcam and mic

• Stable internet for smooth video calls

• A quiet space to work with your camera on

• 20-25 hrs/week available during peak hours (weekday US afternoons/evenings + weekend days)

• You genuinely enjoy talking with both kids and parents

Nice-to-Haves

• Experience in sales, customer service, customer success, tutoring, or coaching

• Experience working with kids and/or parents

• Comfortable managing your own schedule remotely

Highlights
Run engaging 1:1 online trial lessons with US kids, help parents choose the right program, and earn per lesson + bonuses - up to $2,200/mo, part-time, fully remote.

title: Engineering Manager, Rosalind Workbench
description:

Life sciences is one of the clearest areas where advances in intelligence can meaningfully benefit the world at large. The OpenAI Life Sciences team works at the intersection of advancing frontier life sciences model capabilities and building products to help scientists accelerate their research and leverage the full potential of AI for scientific work.

Rosalind Workbench brings together the scientific tools, data sources, interactive biology file viewers and core life sciences workflows into a central environment to help scientists investigate questions, design experiments, analyze results, and advance discovery. Rosalind Workbench can be used with any OpenAI models including GPT-Rosalind, our dedicated life sciences model, which combines frontier reasoning with specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance, and other scientific applications. Our long term vision is for teams of agents to work together across these domains, giving researchers access to broader expertise and the ability to pursue more ambitious scientific questions.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team building Rosalind Workbench and its supporting infrastructure. You’ll hire and develop engineers, set technical direction, and turn an ambitious product roadmap into focused, reliable releases.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You should be comfortable reviewing architecture and code, investigating difficult failures, and helping engineers make consequential technical decisions. You’ll work closely with product, design, research, Codex engineering, and customer-facing teams to bring new scientific capabilities into everyday use.

- Make scientific work inspectable and reproducible. Preserve the inputs, versions, results, and decisions behind an analysis. Ensure scientists can move between conversations, viewers, and follow-up investigations without losing context or control.

- Own engineering quality in production. Establish testing, release practices, observability, and an effective on-call process. Improve workflow reliability, latency, and cost, and lead resolution of problems that prevent scientists from completing their work.

- Coordinate across teams and partners. Align with Codex on shared platform capabilities and with customer-facing engineers on deployment needs. Lead technical decisions about building or integrating scientific tools, specialist models, data sources, and experimental service providers.

- Turn customer learning into reusable improvements. Work directly with scientists and design partners to understand their workflows. Address enterprise requirements such as private compute, credentials, networking, permissions, and data handling, with clear ownership for common product improvements and customer-specific integrations.

- Connect product engineering with research. Help turn capabilities proven in internal research into supported product features. Build instrumentation and feedback pipelines that measure successful workflows and repeat use, and support evaluation and model improvement under explicit consent and data-use requirements.

title: Edge Compute Engineer
description:
AST SpaceMobile is building the first and only global cellular broadband network in space to operate directly with standard, unmodified mobile devices based on our extensive IP and patent portfolio and designed for both commercial and government applications. Our engineers and space scientists are on a mission to eliminate the connectivity gaps faced by today’s five billion mobile subscribers and finally bring broadband to the billions who remain unconnected.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Edge Compute Engineer to join the Latvia Design Center as the primary owner of our ground-segment compute and storage stack running the edge workloads running across all AST ground gateway stations. The Edge Compute Engineer owns the design, provisioning, and lifecycle of this platform across the full gateway fleet globally.

This is a design-and-operate role for a senior engineer who can define the edge compute reference architecture, build an IaC-driven fleet management stack, and take hands-on operational ownership. As the fleet scales, this role will also shape the edge compute platform for future edge functions beyond the current scope.

Key Responsibilities:

• Define and own the edge compute reference architecture: virtualization platform (VMware-based virtualization or Kubernetes), VM/container topology, storage layout, virtual networking, and resource governance across the gateway fleet

• Design the platform to support confirmed edge workloads with headroom and architectural provision for deployment of future edge workloads

• Maintain architecture documentation, platform design records, and operational runbooks

• Build and maintain Terraform-based provisioning pipelines and PXE/TFTP-based boot and instance management for consistent, repeatable gateway node deployment

• Implement Ansible-based configuration management and GitOps workflows to enforce auditable configuration state across all hypervisor nodes remotely

• Manage virtualization cluster operations (VMware-based virtualization or Kubernetes): VM/pod lifecycle, HA, storage pools, virtual networking, and patching automation

• Maintain platform-level observability integrated into the central Prometheus/Grafana/VictoriaMetrics stack and support capacity planning as the fleet expands

• Enforce OS hardening baselines, PKI/certificate lifecycle (IAM Roles Anywhere, mTLS), encrypted storage, and firewall rules aligned with AST’s security governance

• Coordinate with on-site teams or vendors for server firmware, BIOS, and RAID configuration as needed; maintain accurate hardware and software inventory across the fleet

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Telecommunications Engineering, or a related field - or equivalent professional experience.

Experience:

A minimum of 5 to 8 years of hands-on experience in infrastructure or platform engineering, with a strong focus on hypervisor administration, Linux systems, and infrastructure-as-code. Demonstrated experience designing and operating distributed or edge compute environments.

• Deep hands-on VMware-based virtualization or Kubernetes (K8s) - cluster management, HA/DRS, virtual networking, storage pools

• Advanced administration (RHEL, Ubuntu, Debian) - systemd, network stack tuning, performance profiling, security hardening

• Terraform for infrastructure provisioning; PXE/TFTP-based boot and instance management; fleet-scale state management

• Ansible and GitOps workflows for drift-free, pipeline-driven configuration enforcement

• Cisco/Juniper networking (switching/routing), VLANs, VPN (IPsec/WireGuard), PrivateLink/private connectivity, last-mile network management, firewall management

• AWS hybrid cloud - Direct Connect, Site-to-Site VPN, PrivateLink integration with on-premises infrastructure

• Certificate lifecycle management, mTLS, IAM Roles Anywhere, access control for production edge infrastructure

• Prometheus, Grafana, VictoriaMetrics - hypervisor and VM health
